title: Cross-Functional Apprenticeship & Starter Toolkit (2026)
author: Aisha Kumar
summary: A structured 90-day cross-functional apprenticeship program that accelerates new and transitioning contributors through role-specific ladders, integrates benefits orientation, and provides a step-by-step internal tools starter kit. Designed for early-career hires, IC-to-manager rotations, and engineers joining product/platform teams.
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a repeatable apprenticeship flow that combines role clarity, hands-on projects, assigned mentorship, and an internal tools ramp to reduce time-to-impact while preserving predictable career progression and benefits alignment. The program balances people-ops guardrails with team-specific learning plans so hiring managers can onboard contributors with consistent experience and measurable outcomes.

Who this is for:
- New full-time hires (engineers, product, SRE, support)
- Internal transferees rotating between functions (e.g., infra -> platform)
- Early-career apprenticeship hires (cohort-based)

Core objectives:
1. Reduce average time-to-productive-contribution from 90 -> 60 days for apprenticeship participants.
2. Provide a documented ramp that explicitly maps to role ladders and promotion criteria.
3. Ensure tool access and baseline security/compliance checks within first 48 hours.
4. Create measurable mentor/mentee commitments (mentor ratio 1:4; 2 weekly touchpoints).

Program structure (90-day phased plan):
Phase 0 (Pre-start, owner: People Ops, timeline: -7 to 0 days):
- Background checks, equipment provisioning, building access, pre-reads distributed.
- Manager shares 90-day plan and first project brief.
- Tools checklist triggered: Okta invite, GitHub org access request, Slack group, console read-only.

Phase 1 (Foundations, owner: Hiring Manager & Mentor, days 0–30):
- Week 1: orientation, security briefing, team rituals, intro tasks (scaffolded).
- Week 2–4: paired onboarding tasks, runbook walkthroughs, first small PR.
- Deliverable: documented "first-30" retrospective and feature stub merged.

Phase 2 (Applied work, owner: Team Lead, days 31–60):
- Rotating small projects with incremental ownership.
- Midpoint check-in: competency rubric review and benefits Q&A session.
- Deliverable: autonomous ownership of a single service/feature for a sprint.

Phase 3 (Ownership & Career sync, owner: Manager, days 61–90):
- Handover autonomy for maintenance tasks; present outcomes to team.
- Career ladder calibration: map observed competencies to role expectations.
- Deliverable: promotion-readiness note or continued development plan.

Role & Career ladder alignment:
- Each apprenticeship cohort is paired with the published role ladder for the target role.
- Managers must attach the relevant ladder link to the 90-day plan and explicitly call out the 3 promotion-critical behaviors expected at the next level.
- Example mapping (engineer apprentice):
  - Level IC1: deliver small features, write unit tests, follow coding standards.
  - Level IC2: own a service component, lead design discussions, mentor interns.

Access & internal tools starter kit (must complete within 48 hours):
- Required access: Okta SSO, Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, CI dashboard, Datadog (read), JIRA.
- Security: MFA enabled, company laptop encrypted, mandatory secure-coding checklist.
- Tools onboarding items (owners in parentheses):
  1) Okta & Google account setup (people-ops).
  2) GitHub org + repo permissions request (team repo owner).
  3) CI pipeline read-access and local runner config (devops).
  4) Datadog dashboards and alert subscriptions (SRE).
  5) Local dev environment bootstrap script and sample data (team engineering).

Quick-access table: tool, initial permission, owner, SLA
| Tool        | Initial Permission  | Owner       | SLA to grant |
|-------------|---------------------|-------------|---------------|
| Okta        | SSO user            | People Ops  | 4 hours       |
| GitHub      | org+repo read/write | Team Owner  | 8 hours       |
| Datadog     | read dashboard      | SRE         | 24 hours      |
| CI System   | read logs           | DevOps      | 24 hours      |
| Internal Console | read-only       | Platform    | 48 hours      |

Benefits orientation and mapping:
- New hires receive a benefits onboarding session in week 2 covering healthcare, 401(k), paid time off, parental leave, and commuter/office stipends.
- For apprentices and rotational roles, people-ops provides a benefits mapping note that clarifies stipend eligibility and pro-rated time off.
- Sample benefits mapping (ascii table):
| Employment Type | PTO accrual (yr1) | Health plan eligibility | Office stipend |
|-----------------|-------------------|-------------------------|----------------|
| Full-time FTE   | 15 days           | Day 1                   | $400/quarter   |
| Apprenticeship  | 10 days (prorated) | After 30 days           | $200/quarter   |
| Contractor      | N/A               | No (depends on plan)    | No             |

Hiring manager checklist (pre-start to 90 days):
1. Create role-specific 90-day plan and attach role ladder (day -7).
2. Identify and confirm mentor (ratio <= 1:4) and schedule weekly 1:1s (day -3).
3. Complete tool access requests and verify SLAs (day 0).
4. Run weekly progress syncs with people-ops for first 30 days.
5. Conduct midpoint competency calibration at day 45 and record notes.
6. Final career ladder calibration at day 90 and decide next steps.

Mentor expectations:
- Two weekly touchpoints: one technical pairing session (1 hour) and one career/feedback check (30 minutes).
- Provide code reviews within 48 hours for critical PRs.
- Maintain a short growth log (3 bullet outcomes weekly) to share at mid and end checkpoints.

Governance & compliance:
- All apprentices sign the standard Redwood confidentiality and security onboarding forms before system access.
- Any deviation to advantages (extended stipends, accelerated promotion) must be approved by People Ops and documented in the related_pages field.

Success metrics & reporting (owner: People Ops & Hiring Manager):
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (target <= 21 days).
- Time-to-autonomous-ownership (target <= 60 days).
- Mentee satisfaction (pulse survey at days 30/90, target >= 85% positive).
- Mentor load (maintain ratio <= 1:4).

Related resources and templates (appendix):
- 90-day plan template: /confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/90-day-plan-template (link internal).
- Role ladder index: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/role-ladders-index (link internal).
- Tool access request form: /internal/self-service/access-requests (link internal).
- Sample onboarding checklist (text file included in team repo).

FAQ (short):
Q: Can apprentices be converted to FTE?
A: Yes. Conversion follows standard hiring/offer process; manager must submit conversion proposal to People Ops with 90-day outcomes.

Q: What if tool access is delayed beyond SLA?
A: Escalate to the tools-owner channel; People Ops will open a support ticket and provide a temporary sandbox where feasible.

Q: How are promotions considered during apprenticeship?
A: Promotions are possible, but require evidence against the ladder behaviors and a cross-functional calibration panel.

Appendix: templates and checklists are available in the team wiki and referenced related pages above. For questions, contact people-ops@redwood.ai or the program lead, Aisha Kumar.
